candidate_permission_route.name: Microsoft, "Use of Microsoft copyrighted content" guidelines (Screenshots section)
summary_of_terms_read: The guidelines allow screenshots other than boot-up, opening, splash or beta screens to be used in videos, provided the general requirements are also met.
General requirements: use the full product name, link with plain text, make no offensive or disparaging use, and include the statement "Used with permission from Microsoft."

Screenshot conditions: alter only by resizing; do not use portions of screenshots; do not place screenshots in a product UI; do not use screenshots containing third-party content or an identifiable individual.
fit_questions_not_settled_by_evidence: The asset is a figure in Microsoft documentation, not a screenshot captured by the project from a running Microsoft product. Whether the Screenshots section covers reuse of a documentation figure has not been confirmed.
Microsoft itself published only the control's client area (no window frame). The project uses the whole published figure, but a reviewer could read the figure as a portion of a screenshot.

The editorial frame resizes uniformly (integer 2x nearest-neighbour) and adds a background around the image. The pixels inside are unaltered apart from the resize. The later collage (XTRA-14/15) may overlap, crop or rotate it, which the "alter only by resizing" condition would forbid.
The sample name "Peter Rabbit" is a literary character name used as dummy data. It is not a depicted person, but it is noted in case it counts as third-party content.
The guidelines advise consulting a copyright attorney for questions. No legal review has been done.

access_terms: Public anonymous page on learn.microsoft.com. No terms were clicked through, no account used, no payment made.
credit_text: Microsoft Corporation, "Developing Applications with the Microsoft Visual Basic 6.0 Data Object Wizard," Figure 16 (December 1998). Used with permission from Microsoft.
credit_text_note: The "Used with permission from Microsoft" clause is correct only if the reviewer accepts that the Microsoft guidelines apply. Otherwise use the credit without that sentence and keep release blocked.
handoff: Review question XTRA-12-RQ1 in evidence/claim-checks.json. Devin decides whether the Microsoft screenshot guidelines cover this documentation figure as used in the video and in the XTRA-14/15 collage, or whether written permission or a substitute is needed.
